unit.title: Change of State: The Translative Case

stories.summary: Carlos and his friend Zoltán renovate an old storage room into a cozy community workshop and café space.

stories.title: Önkéntesként a táborban
stories.summary: Carlos and Eszter spend a week as volunteers organizing activities at a youth summer camp near the Danube Bend.

stories.title: Névnap a nagymamánál
stories.summary: Carlos attends a traditional Hungarian Name Day celebration for Eszter's grandmother, learning visiting etiquette, toasting, and respectful deferential language.

stories.title: Az út, amit sosem felejtek el
stories.summary: A first-person account of a hiking trip in the Bakony hills that turns into an unexpected storm, a shelter, and a story worth remembering.

stories.title: Élmények, amik megváltoztattak
stories.summary: A first-person reflection on the experiences of the last ten years — a first solo trip abroad, learning to cook from a grandmother, and looking back at how much the narrator has changed.

stories.title: János vitéz útja
stories.summary: An adapted retelling of the opening of Petőfi's folk epic János vitéz: an orphaned goose-herd loses his geese, is driven from home, says goodbye to the girl he loves, and sets out to become a soldier.
stories.author: Sándor Petőfi

stories.title: Hét krajcár
stories.summary: An adapted retelling of Zsigmond Móricz's short story: an adult narrator remembers a poor but warm childhood afternoon spent with his mother, searching the house for seven missing krajcárs.
stories.author: Zsigmond Móricz

stories.title: Az arany ember
stories.summary: An adapted retelling of Mór Jókai's novel Az arany ember: a poor young riverboat worker, Tímár Mihály, rises to become a wealthy, respected merchant through careful planning, hard work and perseverance.
stories.author: Mór Jókai

stories.title: Bede Anna tartozása
stories.summary: An adapted retelling of Kálmán Mikszáth's short story: a grieving widow receives a bureaucratic demand to pay her late daughter's small old debt, and the village notary must decide how to advise and help her.
stories.author: Kálmán Mikszáth

stories.title: Nyilas Misi és a barátság próbája
stories.summary: An adapted retelling inspired by Zsigmond Móricz's novel Légy jó mindhalálig: a poor scholarship boy at the Debrecen boarding school is entrusted with money that goes missing, and must rebuild the trust of his closest friend and classmates despite the injustice.
stories.author: Zsigmond Móricz

stories.title: Kopjáss István és az új állás
stories.summary: An adapted retelling inspired by Zsigmond Móricz's classic novel Rokonok: Kopjáss István unexpectedly wins election to a prestigious town leadership post, confronting sudden career elevation, new responsibilities, and a swarm of relatives seeking office favours.
stories.author: Zsigmond Móricz

stories.title: A rossz tanuló felel
stories.summary: An adapted retelling inspired by Frigyes Karinthy's humorous masterpiece Tanár úr kérem: an unprepared student is called up to the blackboard, experiencing the universal drama of school oral examination and attempting to bluff his way through.
stories.author: Frigyes Karinthy

stories.title: A glogovai utazás
stories.summary: An adapted retelling inspired by Kálmán Mikszáth's beloved classic novel Szent Péter esernyője: travelers journey by carriage through the rugged northern mountains and muddy roads toward Glogova, pursuing the mysterious umbrella said to hold miraculous fortunes.
stories.author: Kálmán Mikszáth

stories.title: Esti Kornél és az orvosi vizsgálat
stories.summary: An adapted retelling inspired by Dezső Kosztolányi's witty literary masterpiece Esti Kornél: Esti visits an elderly, experienced professor for a medical checkup, reflecting on human vulnerability, the art of reassurance, and the profound connection between bodily health and peace of mind.
stories.author: Dezső Kosztolányi

stories.title: Édes Anna a Krisztinavárosban
stories.summary: In this adapted excerpt from Dezső Kosztolányi's masterpiece Édes Anna, Mrs. Vizy meticulously inspects the spotless bourgeois flat in Krisztinaváros before the quiet country girl Anna steps across the threshold into her new home.

stories.title: Nyilas Misi Debrecen városában
stories.summary: In this adapted literary excerpt from Zsigmond Móricz's beloved classic Légy jó mindhalálig, young student Misi navigates the historic streets and proud civic community of Debrecen, learning responsibility as he visits the blind old gentleman Mr. Pósalaky.

stories.title: Szindbád és a vasárnapi ebéd
stories.summary: In this adapted excerpt from Gyula Krúdy's world-famous Szindbád stories, the nostalgic traveler Szindbád savors the sacred ritual of Sunday lunch in a quiet old-world tavern, contemplating the steaming golden broth, marrow bones, and freshly grated horseradish.

stories.title: A vörösingesek követe és a kiáltvány a grundon
stories.summary: An adaptation from Ferenc Molnár's immortal classic novel 'A Pál utcai fiúk'. On the Paul Street playground, Boka and his friends receive startling news: the rival Redshirts intend to conquer their lot. Boka drafts an official proclamation and posts it for everyone to read.
stories.author: Molnár Ferenc

stories.title: A delejes gépember és a jövő masinái
stories.location: Budapest, New York kávéház és műhely
stories.summary: An adaptation inspired by the visionary satirical writings of Frigyes Karinthy on technology, thinking machines, and communication. Karinthy visits an eccentric inventor's workshop in Budapest, where a thinking metal machine attempts to write poetry.
stories.author: Karinthy Frigyes
stories.work: Így írtok ti / Tanár úr kérem és egyéb tárcák

stories.title: A bécsi színházban és a bál forgatagában
stories.summary: An adaptation from Mór Jókai's masterwork 'A kőszívű ember fiai' (The Baron's Sons). In glamorous imperial Vienna, young Ödön and Richard Baradlay attend the opera and the grand charity ball, experiencing the heights of high society, theater, music, and the gathering storm of Hungarian patriotism.
stories.author: Jókai Mór

stories.title: A lámpás és az erdő csendje
stories.summary: An adaptation from Géza Gárdonyi's celebrated writings on Hungarian village nature and forests. The village teacher walks through the ancient Bakony forest at twilight, reflecting on the beauty of nature, the harmony of living creatures, and mankind's sacred duty to protect the woods.
stories.author: Gárdonyi Géza

stories.title: A fillér értéke és az emberség
stories.summary: An adaptation from Zsigmond Móricz's heart-rending stories of social realism ('Hét krajcár'). In a small, modest home, a mother and her young son search every corner for seven lost pennies to buy soap to wash clothes, turning hardship into a moment of pure laughter, solidarity, and indestructible human dignity.
stories.author: Móricz Zsigmond

stories.title: A képviselő úr választási beszéde
stories.summary: An adaptation from Kálmán Mikszáth's satirical masterpieces on Hungarian parliamentary politics and election campaigns ('A képviselő úr'). In a small county town, the aspiring MP delivers a grand, flowery speech promising golden bridges and prosperity, while the sensible townspeople listen with wry humor and shrewd common sense.
stories.author: Mikszáth Kálmán

stories.title: A gavallérok és a bankhitel
stories.summary: An adaptation inspired by Kálmán Mikszáth's sharp satirical masterpiece 'A gavallérok' (The Cavaliers). In the 19th-century Hungarian countryside, aristocratic gentlemen who live beyond their means gather at the county fair, attempting to negotiate loans and keep up the appearance of wealth with wit, charm, and empty pockets.
stories.author: Mikszáth Kálmán

stories.title: Károly Róbert és a gazdasági rend
stories.summary: Following the extinction of the Árpád dynasty, Charles Robert of Anjou restored central authority in Hungary, broke the power of the oligarchs, and created economic prosperity with Europe's most famous gold florin.

stories.title: A visegrádi királytalálkozó
stories.summary: In 1335, Charles Robert hosted a historic diplomatic congress in the royal palace of Visegrád with the kings of Bohemia and Poland, forging alliances and opening new trade routes.

stories.title: Nagy Lajos és az 1351-es törvények
stories.summary: King Louis the Great, celebrated as a chivalric monarch, expanded Hungary's power across Poland and Italy and enshrined fundamental noble liberties in the 1351 laws.

stories.title: Zsigmond és a déli végvárrendszer
stories.summary: Sigismund of Luxembourg, king of Hungary and Holy Roman Emperor, recognized the rising Ottoman peril and pioneered a formidable double chain of border fortresses.

stories.title: Hunyadi János és a nándorfehérvári diadal
stories.summary: In July 1456, governor János Hunyadi and crusader friar John of Capistrano repelled Mehmed II's siege of Belgrade, securing Hungary and inspiring the worldwide midday church bell decree.

stories.title: Az Anjouk és a középkori királyok
stories.summary: The complete chronological saga of 14th and 15th century Hungary: from Charles Robert's financial revival and the 1335 Visegrád summit to Louis the Great's knightly empire, Sigismund's border fortifications, and Hunyadi's immortal victory at Nándorfehérvár in 1456.

stories.title: Az Árpád-házi királyok
stories.summary: After István, the House of Árpád kept the Hungarian throne for nearly three centuries: I. László the border-defender, Könyves Kálmán the scholar-king, and II. András, whose reign set the stage for the Golden Bull.

stories.title: Az Aranybulla
stories.summary: Why the nobility pressed II. András for a written charter, what the Golden Bull of 1222 actually guaranteed, and why historians compare it to England's Magna Carta.
topics: aki és amely: személyek és dolgok

stories.title: Az ország megszervezése
stories.summary: The county system that governed the kingdom, the catastrophe of the 1241-42 Mongol invasion, and IV. Béla's stone-castle rebuilding programme afterward.
topics: a vonatkozó névmás esetei: akit, akinek, akik

stories.title: Egyház és állam
stories.summary: How the church's dioceses and monasteries were organized alongside the kingdom, the 1083 canonizations, and the church's economic and political role.
topics: ahol és amikor: hely- és időhatározói mellékmondatok

stories.title: Az Árpád-ház vége
stories.summary: The weakening of royal power under the last Árpád kings, III. András's brief reign, and the male line's extinction in 1301.

stories.title: Az Árpád-ház
stories.summary: A synthesis of the Árpád dynasty's nearly four-century rule after István: notable kings, the Golden Bull of 1222, the kingdom's consolidation through the tatárjárás, church and state, and the male line's extinction in 1301.
topics: aki és amely: személyek és dolgok

stories.title: A fejedelemség megszületése
stories.summary: Following Buda's fall in 1541, Queen Isabella and her infant son John Sigismund established the autonomous Principality of Transylvania in Gyulafehérvár, paying tribute to the sultan while maintaining internal Hungarian statehood.

stories.title: A tordai vallásbéke (1568)
stories.summary: At the 1568 Diet of Torda, Transylvania enacted Europe's first law on universal religious tolerance, granting equal legal protection to Catholic, Lutheran, Reformed, and Unitarian believers amid bloody religious wars across the continent.

stories.title: Bethlen Gábor és a gazdasági felvirágzás
stories.summary: Prince Gábor Bethlen (1613–1629) ushered in Transylvania's Golden Age through state monopolies on salt and mining, attracting skilled foreign craftsmen and founding the illustrious princely academy in Gyulafehérvár.

stories.title: Erdély a harmincéves háborúban
stories.summary: During the Thirty Years' War, Bethlen Gábor allied with Protestant European powers against the Habsburg Emperor, capturing Upper Hungary and securing constitutional freedoms in the 1621 Peace of Nikolsburg.

stories.title: A magyar nyelv és kultúra menedéke
stories.summary: While the central plains suffered Ottoman devastation, Transylvania flourished as the sanctuary of Hungarian literature, vernacular education, and psalm translation, cementing the enduring foundation of modern national consciousness.

stories.title: Erdély aranykora és történelmi öröksége
stories.summary: The glorious golden age of the Principality of Transylvania: its establishment after Buda's fall in 1541, the revolutionary 1568 Diet of Torda proclaiming universal religious freedom, Prince Gábor Bethlen's mercantilist economic boom and academic patronage, participation in the Thirty Years' War, and its enduring role as the cultural sanctuary of the Hungarian language.

stories.title: Eső és forradalom Pesten
stories.summary: March 15, 1848 begins on a cold, pouring morning in Pest. Petőfi and the March Youth gather at the Pilvax coffee house, marching through wet cobblestone streets to Landerer's printing press to seize freedom of the press without shedding a drop of blood.

stories.title: Mit kíván a magyar nemzet?
stories.summary: On the afternoon of March 15, thousands gather outside the National Museum in the rain. Vasvári and Jókai read out the Twelve Points: an independent ministry, emancipation of the serfs, equality before the law, and the release of political prisoner Táncsics.

stories.title: A törvényes forradalom és a függetlenség
stories.summary: Batthyány forms Hungary's first responsible government, and the April Laws transform the kingdom into a modern civic state. But when the Habsburg court attacks, the parliament retreats to Debrecen, where Kossuth proclaims full independence in the Great Church.

stories.title: A tavaszi hadjárat csodája
stories.summary: The young Honvéd army, led by the brilliant Artúr Görgei, performs miracles during the Spring Campaign of 1849. At Hatvan, Tápióbicske, and Isaszeg, the Hungarian forces smash the imperial armies and retake Buda, terrifying Vienna.

stories.title: Világos és az aradi vértanúk öröksége
stories.summary: Faced with overwhelming Austrian and Russian forces, Görgei lays down arms at Világos before the Russian general. The brutal Austrian retribution executes Batthyány and the Thirteen Martyrs at Arad, turning their sacrifice into the eternal cornerstone of Hungarian liberty.

stories.title: Az 1848–49-es forradalom és szabadságharc
stories.summary: The epic story of 1848–49: from the rainy morning at Pilvax and the Twelve Points, through the April Laws and Kossuth's proclamation in Debrecen, to the glorious Spring Campaign and the tragic sacrifice of the Arad Martyrs.

stories.title: A Királyi Magyarország és Pozsony
stories.summary: Following Mohács and the fall of Buda, the northern and western parts of Hungary came under Habsburg rule as Royal Hungary, with Pozsony (Bratislava) serving as the kingdom's coronation capital and administrative center.

stories.title: Buda 1541-es elfoglalása és a Hódoltság
stories.summary: On August 29, 1541, Sultan Suleiman captured Buda Castle through trickery without firing a shot, establishing the Ottoman-ruled territory (Hódoltság) across the heart of Hungary for 150 years.

stories.title: Erdély: A magyar kultúra és a vallásszabadság bástyája
stories.summary: In the east, the Principality of Transylvania arose under John Sigismund and later princes. Headquartered in Gyulafehérvár, Transylvania preserved Hungarian language and enacted Europe's first law on religious tolerance in 1568.

stories.title: Végvári élet és mezővárosi virágzás a határokon
stories.summary: Along the border fortress chain (Eger, Szigetvár, Győr), heroic border warriors fought daily skirmishes. Concurrently, the agricultural market towns of the Great Plain grew wealthy trading Hungarian grey cattle to western Europe.

stories.title: Másfél évszázad megosztottságban
stories.summary: Between 1541 and 1699, Hungary endured 150 years of tripartite division. Despite widespread destruction, the legal unity of the Hungarian crown, culture, and language endured until Buda's liberation in 1686.

stories.title: A három részre szakadt Magyarország (1541–1699)
stories.summary: The dramatic 150-year era of the tripartite partition of Hungary (1541–1699): Royal Hungary under Habsburg rule with Pozsony as capital, the Ottoman Hódoltság centered in Buda, the autonomous Principality of Transylvania championing religious freedom, heroic border fortress defense, cattle trade, and the eventual liberation of Buda in 1686.

stories.title: Miért indultak nyugatra a magyar törzsek
stories.summary: Why, after centuries on the Pontic steppe, mounting pressure from the Pechenegs forced the Magyar tribal confederation to abandon Etelköz and set out west toward the Carpathians.
topics: Miért indultak nyugatra a magyar törzsek

stories.title: Átkelés a Kárpátokon
stories.summary: How the Magyar tribes crossed the Carpathian mountains around 895, traditionally through the Verecke Pass, and what let their light cavalry and archers move so effectively.

stories.title: Árpád és a hét törzs
stories.summary: How the seven Magyar tribes, according to tradition, united under a blood oath and were led into the new homeland by Árpád, founder of the ruling Árpád dynasty.
topics: nevesített alanyok: Árpád és a hét törzs

stories.title: A medence birtokba vétele
stories.summary: How the Magyar tribes gradually occupied the Carpathian Basin over several years, absorbing or displacing the peoples already there, and secured their new home at the Battle of Pozsony in 907.

stories.title: A honfoglalás a nemzeti emlékezetben
stories.summary: Why 895 and the honfoglalás remain central to Hungarian national identity today, from the turul bird and the Csodaszarvas legend to the Millennium Monument — and why it matters for the citizenship exam.
topics: összefoglalás: miután, mielőtt és több szereplő

stories.title: A honfoglalás (895)
stories.summary: The full story of the honfoglalás: why the Magyar tribes left the steppe, how they crossed the Carpathians under Árpád and the seven tribes, how they settled the basin, and why 895 still matters to Hungarian national identity today.
topics: nevesített alanyok: Árpád és a hét törzs
összefoglalás: miután, mielőtt és több szereplő

unit.title: Saint Stephen & the Founding of the State (1000)

stories.summary: How Prince Géza turned the Magyars toward Christian Europe, had himself and his son baptized, and prepared the ground for his son István's coronation as king.
topics: Géza fejedelem és a kereszténység felé fordulás

stories.title: István koronázása

unit.title: Saint Stephen & the Founding of the State (1000)

stories.summary: How István defeated the pagan chieftain Koppány after Géza's death, and was crowned the first King of Hungary around the year 1000 with a crown tradition says was sent by Pope Sylvester II.

stories.title: Keresztény királyság építése

unit.title: Saint Stephen & the Founding of the State (1000)

stories.summary: How István organized the Hungarian church into an archbishopric and ten dioceses, founded monasteries, and passed laws establishing a functioning Christian kingdom.

stories.title: Szent István öröksége

unit.title: Saint Stephen & the Founding of the State (1000)

stories.summary: István's Intelmek (Admonitions) to his son Imre, the succession crisis after Imre's early death, and István's canonization in 1083 as Hungary's patron saint.

stories.title: A Szent Korona

unit.title: Saint Stephen & the Founding of the State (1000)

stories.summary: The Holy Crown and the rest of the coronation regalia, the crown's eventful modern history, and what it symbolizes today as the continuity of Hungarian statehood.

stories.title: Szent István és az államalapítás

unit.title: Saint Stephen & the Founding of the State (1000)

stories.summary: A synthesis of Szent István's story — Géza's turn to Christianity, Koppány's defeat, István's coronation around the year 1000, the Christian kingdom he built, his legacy and canonization, and the Holy Crown that still symbolizes Hungarian statehood today.

stories.title: A medence korai népei

unit.title: The Carpathian Basin Before the Magyars

stories.summary: Who lived in the Carpathian Basin long before the Magyars arrived: the Illyrian-related Pannon tribes, then the Celtic peoples who settled and left their mark on the land.

stories.summary: How Rome conquered the western Carpathian Basin, built cities and roads across the province of Pannonia, and eventually withdrew after four centuries.

unit.title: The Carpathian Basin Before the Magyars

stories.summary: The Migration Period in the Carpathian Basin: the Huns, the collapse of Attila's empire, the Goths and other peoples who followed, and the Avars who ruled the basin for two and a half centuries alongside Slavic settlement.

stories.title: Kik éltek itt korábban?

unit.title: The Carpathian Basin Before the Magyars

stories.summary: A summary of everyone who lived in the Carpathian Basin before the Magyars — one after another and sometimes at the same time — and why none of them ever unified the whole basin.

unit.title: The Carpathian Basin Before the Magyars

stories.summary: Why, by the late 9th century, no single power controlled the Carpathian Basin — and why that made it the stage for a new arrival: the Magyar tribes, around 895.

unit.title: The Carpathian Basin Before the Magyars

stories.summary: A synthesis of the Carpathian Basin's long history before 895 — Pannon and Celtic tribes, Roman Pannonia, the Migration Period's Huns, Goths, Avars and Slavs — and why the basin lay open for the Magyar tribes to arrive.
topics: több szereplő a múlt idejű elbeszélésben
sorrend a történelemben: korábban, majd, végül

stories.title: A csendes dac és a passzív ellenállás
stories.summary: Following the tragic defeat of 1849, the Austrian minister Alexander Bach installs a suffocating police bureaucracy. But Hungarians invent passive resistance: refusing to speak German, ignoring imperial decrees, and practicing stubborn tax refusal while wearing traditional Hungarian coats.

stories.title: A Haza Bölcse és a Húsvéti cikk
stories.summary: Ferenc Deák, residing in the modest Queen of England Hotel in Pest, carves wooden boxes, smokes his pipe, and bides his time. On Easter 1865, he pens the legendary Easter Article in Pesti Napló, offering a brilliant, realistic compromise based on the 1723 Pragmatic Sanction.

stories.title: A koronázás fényei és Erzsébet királyné
stories.summary: On June 8, 1867, Budapest witnesses one of the most dazzling spectacles in European history. In the Matthias Church, Franz Joseph is crowned with Saint Stephen's Crown, while the beloved Queen Elisabeth ('Sisi'), wearing a dress by Charles Worth, seals the reconciliation.

stories.title: A dualizmus világa: Közös ügyek és önállóság
stories.summary: The Austro-Hungarian Monarchy is established as a unique dual-state superpower. Emperor Franz Joseph reigns over both halves, foreign affairs and the army are managed jointly, but in Pest, a sovereign parliament and prime minister govern Hungarian domestic destiny.

stories.title: A gazdasági robbanás és a jogfolytonosság
stories.summary: With peace secured, Hungary experiences an unprecedented economic explosion. Capital pours into railways, banks, and factories; Buda and Pest unite into Budapest in 1873. The historical legacy of 1867 preserved the continuity of Hungarian constitutional law.

stories.title: A kiegyezés és a dualizmus születése
stories.summary: From the stubborn passive resistance of the Bach era and Deák's masterly Easter Article, to the glittering coronation of Franz Joseph and Sisi in 1867, and the golden decades of economic growth that transformed Budapest into a world metropolis.

stories.title: Az ország újranépesítése a 18. században
stories.summary: How the devastated plains of Hungary were repopulated after the Ottoman wars by German Swabians, Slovaks, and Serbs, creating a colorful multinational state.

stories.title: Mária Terézia és az 1741-es pozsonyi országgyűlés
stories.summary: The dramatic moment in Pozsony when the Hungarian nobility drew their swords for Maria Theresa with the famous cry: 'Vitam et sanguinem!'

stories.title: Felvilágosult reformok: Urbárium és Ratio Educationis
stories.summary: Maria Theresa's enlightened decrees: the Urbarium limiting feudal peasant labor, and the Ratio Educationis establishing modern primary education.

stories.title: II. József, a kalapos király és rendeletei
stories.summary: Joseph II's controversial rule by decree: the progressive Edict of Tolerance, the resented German language decree, and his deathbed revocations.

stories.title: Nemzeti ébredés és a magyar nyelv mozgalma
stories.summary: How noble resistance to Germanization sparked the mother-tongue revival, György Bessenyei's writings, and the birth of modern Hungarian national identity.

stories.title: A 18. század: újjáépítés és felvilágosodás
stories.summary: The comprehensive saga of 18th-century Hungary: repopulation, Maria Theresa's enlightened absolutism, Joseph II's decrees, and the dawn of national awakening.

stories.title: Mátyás megválasztása a Duna jegén
stories.summary: In January 1458, the Hungarian nobility gathered on the frozen Danube beneath Buda Castle to elect the young Matthias Corvinus, son of hero János Hunyadi, to the throne.

stories.title: A fekete sereg és a hadviselés
stories.summary: King Matthias established the legendary Black Army, one of Europe's first permanent professional standing armies, securing borders against Ottoman raids and conquering Vienna.

stories.title: A reneszánsz udvar és a Corvina
stories.summary: Under Matthias and Queen Beatrice of Aragon, the royal courts at Buda and Visegrád became Europe's foremost Renaissance centers north of the Alps, home to the famous Corvina library.

stories.title: Mátyás király és az igazságos bíráskodás
stories.summary: Known as 'Matthias the Just', the king modernized taxation through the chimney tax (füstpénz) and entered national folklore as the disguised monarch defending the common folk.

stories.title: Meghalt Mátyás, oda az igazság
stories.summary: When King Matthias died in Vienna in 1490 without a legitimate heir, Hungary entered rapid political fragmentation, crystallizing the enduring proverb 'King Matthias is dead, justice has perished.'

stories.title: Mátyás király és a reneszánsz udvar
stories.summary: The grand historical arc of Renaissance Hungary under King Matthias Corvinus (1458–1490): his dramatic Danube election, the invincible Black Army, European Renaissance patronage and the Corvina library, the legend of 'Matthias the Just', and the national grief following his sudden death in 1490.

stories.title: A meggyengült királyság és a belső viszályok
stories.summary: Following King Matthias's death in 1490, royal central power collapsed under the Jagiellon kings. The brutal suppression of the 1514 Dózsa peasant revolt left Hungarian society deeply divided on the eve of the Ottoman invasion.

stories.title: Szulejmán szultán és Nándorfehérvár eleste
stories.summary: In 1520, the ambitious young Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent came to power in Istanbul. In 1521, the key southern stronghold Nándorfehérvár fell, leaving the Hungarian heartland completely exposed.

stories.title: A tragikus ütközet 1526. augusztus 29-én
stories.summary: On August 29, 1526, on the plains south of Mohács, King Louis II's 25,000 soldiers confronted Sultan Suleiman's 60,000-strong army. Despite a valiant cavalry assault, the Hungarian lines were pulverized by Ottoman cannons within two hours.

stories.title: II. Lajos tragédiája a Csele-patakban
stories.summary: While escaping the battlefield in the stormy dusk, the twenty-year-old King Louis II drowned in the flooded Csele brook when his armored horse stumbled, extinguishing the royal line and throwing Hungary into civil strife.

stories.title: Több is veszett Mohácsnál: A nemzeti emlékezet
stories.summary: The disaster at Mohács in 1526 ended medieval Hungarian great-power status and led to the 150-year Ottoman occupation. It permanently entered national consciousness as the supreme benchmark of tragedy and resilience.

stories.title: A mohácsi csata és a középkori Magyarország bukása
stories.summary: The catastrophic collapse of medieval Hungary at the Battle of Mohács (August 29, 1526): internal disunity after 1514, the rise of Suleiman I and fall of Nándorfehérvár, the two-hour collapse against Ottoman artillery, the drowning of King Louis II in the Csele brook, and the enduring cultural memory encapsulated in 'Több is veszett Mohácsnál'.

stories.title: A kétfejű sas és a Szent Korona
stories.summary: In Rest is History style, we explore the extraordinary bureaucratic and military machinery of the Austro-Hungarian Empire: two sovereign states under one emperor-king, three joint ministries, and a sprawling multinational army speaking a dozen languages.

stories.title: 1896: A birodalom csúcsán – A Millennium
characters: Ybl Miklós és Steindl Imre építészek
stories.summary: Budapest throws the party of the century in 1896 to celebrate the 1000th anniversary of the Hungarian Conquest. From the monumental Heroes' Square to Europe's first underground railway, the kingdom demonstrates its pride and dizzying progress to the world.

stories.title: A kávéházak és paloták városa
stories.location: Budapest, New York Kávéház, Nagykörút, Duna-part
stories.summary: How Pest, Buda and Óbuda merged to become one of the fastest-growing world metropolises. The construction of the Parliament, the sweep of the Grand Boulevard, and the rich coffeehouse culture where literature, journalism and romance flourished.

stories.title: A gőzmalmok és vasutak országa
stories.summary: Behind the glamorous coffeehouses lay industrial might: Budapest was the flour milling capital of the globe, Ganz engineering powered locomotives and European power grids, and an immense railway boom transformed the Hungarian plains into a breadbasket.

stories.title: A boldog békeidők alkonya
stories.summary: As the turn of the century arrived, the golden age of the Belle Époque began to reveal profound tensions. Rural poverty drove hundreds of thousands to emigrate to America, ethnic minorities demanded autonomy, and Europe's old order drifted toward the catastrophe of 1914.

stories.title: Az Osztrák–Magyar Monarchia kora (1867–1914)
characters: Andrássy Gyula és Tisza Kálmán miniszterelnökök
Mechwart András és Steindl Imre alkotók
stories.summary: A comprehensive Rest is History narrative tracing the dual monarchy from the power-sharing compromise to the 1896 Millennium mega-celebration, Budapest's golden age of coffeehouses and heavy industry, and the poignant sunset of the Belle Époque.

stories.title: Kossuth Lajos Amerikában és a világban
stories.summary: After the defeat of 1849, Kossuth escapes to the Ottoman Empire and embarks on a historic tour across Great Britain and America. Speaking in rich, Shakespearean English, his oratorical brilliance enchants hundreds of thousands, turning him into a global champion of liberty.

stories.title: Petőfi Sándor, a lánglelkű költő
stories.summary: Petőfi Sándor lived like a comet: passionate, uncompromising, and dedicated to the people. He wrote masterpieces on rickety tavern tables and insisted on riding to the frontline in Transylvania under General Bem, meeting a mysterious heroic death at Segesvár.

stories.title: A Nemzeti dal születése és hatalma
stories.summary: How Petőfi wrote the immortal 'Nemzeti dal' just days before March 15. The thunderous opening line 'Talpra magyar, hí a haza!' and the collective oath 'Esküszünk, esküszünk!' became the battle-cry of a whole nation that echoes across Hungarian history.

stories.title: Kokárda a szívek felett: Nemzeti jelképeink
stories.summary: The origins of Hungary's beloved national symbols: how Szendrey Júlia sewed the first tricolor cockade for Petőfi, the deep meaning of the red-white-green colors, and the debate between the Holy Crown and the republican Kossuth coat of arms.

stories.title: Március 15.: Miért ünnepel a nemzet?
stories.summary: March 15 is one of Hungary's three official national holidays and a central topic on the citizenship interview. Across cities and diaspora communities, citizens pin cockades, lay wreaths at Petőfi statues, and celebrate the birth of modern civic Hungary.

stories.title: Kossuth, Petőfi és a nemzeti szimbólumok
stories.summary: The heroes and symbols of 1848: Kossuth's global crusade in exile, Petőfi's blazing poetry and sacrifice at Segesvár, the electric vow of the Nemzeti dal, the tricolor cockade, and the lasting meaning of March 15 in modern Hungarian civic life.

stories.title: Hol van Magyarország?
stories.summary: Where Hungary lies, how big it is, and why Hungarian belongs to a language family almost none of its neighbours share.

stories.title: Megyék, folyók és városok
stories.summary: Hungary's nineteen counties, its two great rivers, the Great Plain and Transdanubia, Lake Balaton, and the country's major cities beyond Budapest.

stories.title: A zászló és a címer
stories.summary: The red-white-green flag and its traditional meaning, the Árpád stripes and triple mound on the coat of arms, and the Holy Crown that has watched over Hungarian statehood for a thousand years.

stories.title: Magyarország szomszédai
stories.summary: Hungary's seven neighbours, roughly where each one lies, which are inside the EU and Schengen area, and why Hungarian minorities live across several of these borders today.

stories.title: Első áttekintés
stories.summary: Why this basic geography and these symbols are exactly what a honosítási vizsga interview asks about, and how location, counties, rivers, symbols and neighbours all fit into one first picture of Hungary.

stories.title: Magyarország ma
stories.summary: A synthesis of Hungary's geography, counties and rivers, national symbols, and neighbouring countries — the basic picture of the country that opens the Citizenship track.
topics: Magyarország ma: az ország és jelképei

stories.title: II. Rákóczi Ferenc és a Brezáni kiáltvány
stories.summary: How Prince Ferenc Rákóczi II, the wealthiest landowner in Hungary, answered the call of the peasants and launched the war of independence from Brezán Castle in 1703.

stories.title: A kurucok felkelése és hadviselése
stories.summary: The rapid spread of the Kuruc uprising, light cavalry tactics, the melancholy music of the tárogató, and the liberation of Hungarian territories from the Labanc troops.

stories.title: Az ónodi országgyűlés és a trónfosztás
stories.summary: The dramatic 1707 Diet of Ónód: declaring the dethronement of the Habsburgs, introducing taxation for nobles, copper money inflation, and the turn of military fortune at Trencsén.

stories.title: A szatmári béke és a megbékélés
stories.summary: The 1711 Peace of Szatmár: Count Sándor Károlyi negotiates an honorable compromise that preserves Hungarian constitutional rights and gives general amnesty.

stories.title: Rodostó és a nemzeti emlékezet
stories.summary: Rákóczi's dignified exile in the Turkish town of Rodostó, Kelemen Mikes's famous letters, and how Rákóczi's memory became an eternal pillar of Hungarian patriotism.

stories.title: A Rákóczi-szabadságharc (1703–1711)
stories.summary: The complete historical saga of Rákóczi's War of Independence: from the Brezán proclamation to the Diet of Ónód, the Szatmár compromise, and the immortal exile at Rodostó.

stories.title: Széchenyi István, a legnagyobb magyar
stories.summary: How Count István Széchenyi offered one year of his income to found the Academy of Sciences and published 'Hitel' (Credit), launching the Reform Era.

stories.title: A Lánchíd és a korszerű modernizáció
stories.summary: The construction of the Chain Bridge linking Buda and Pest, Danube river regulation, steam shipping, and breaking the nobility's ancient tax exemption.

stories.title: Kossuth Lajos és a független politikai sajtó
stories.summary: Lajos Kossuth's courageous journalism: evading Habsburg censorship with handwritten parliamentary reports, editing Pesti Hírlap, and championing serf emancipation.

stories.title: A magyar nyelv diadala és nemzeti jelképei
stories.summary: The landmark 1844 language law making Hungarian the official state language, Kölcsey's Himnusz, Vörösmarty's Szózat, and the founding of the National Theatre.

stories.title: A forradalom küszöbén: a Pilvax és a márciusi ifjak
stories.summary: The electric atmosphere on the eve of March 1848: the Védegylet, young radicals at the Pilvax café, European uprisings, and the threshold of revolution.

stories.title: A reformkor (1825–1848)
stories.summary: The magnificent saga of the Hungarian Reform Era: Széchenyi's foundational vision, the Chain Bridge, Kossuth's political press, the 1844 language act, and the eve of 1848.

stories.title: A tatárok közeledése
stories.summary: In the late 1230s, Friar Julian brought dire news from the East: the unstoppable Mongol armies were advancing toward Europe. King Béla IV attempted to prepare the kingdom and welcomed Cuman refugees, but faced deep suspicion from Hungarian nobles.

stories.title: A muhi csata
stories.summary: On 11 April 1241, the royal army clashed with Batu Khan's forces by the Sajó River at Mohi. Despite initial defense of the bridge, the Mongols outflanked the fortified wagon camp, resulting in a crushing defeat for Hungary.

stories.title: Egy elpusztult ország
stories.summary: Throughout 1241 and 1242, the Mongols laid waste to the country. After the Danube froze in winter, they crossed to Transdanubia, sacking unprotected settlements while King Béla fled all the way to Trau on the Adriatic coast.

stories.title: IV. Béla és az újjáépítés
stories.summary: In spring 1242, the Mongols unexpectedly withdrew. King Béla returned to a ruined kingdom and initiated sweeping reforms: inviting settlers, returning Cumans, and earning the historical title of 'Second Founder of the State'.

stories.title: A kővárak országa
stories.summary: The main lesson of 1241 was that wooden earthworks and open towns burned, while stone castles held out. Béla IV launched a massive fortification campaign, founding Buda Castle and building Visegrád, creating a medieval defense network.

stories.title: A tatárjárás és az ország újjáépítése (1241–1242)
stories.summary: The full historical overview of the Mongol invasion of Hungary in 1241-1242: Julian's warning, the disaster at Mohi, the devastating winter of destruction, Béla IV's flight to Trau, and the king's visionary reconstruction program of stone castles.

stories.title: Buda visszavétele 1686-ban
stories.summary: In the summer of 1686, the multinational Christian army of the Holy League besieged Buda. On September 2, 1686, led by Hungarian hero Dávid Petneházy, allied troops stormed the ramparts, ending 145 years of Ottoman rule in the ancient capital.

stories.title: A győzelmes hadjáratok és a karlócai béke
stories.summary: Following Buda's fall, allied forces crushed the Ottomans at Nagyharsány (1687) and Zenta (1697) under Eugene of Savoy. The 1699 Peace of Karlowitz formally ended Ottoman occupation across virtually all of historic Hungary.

stories.title: A felszabadulás súlyos ára
stories.summary: Liberation came at immense human and material cost: scorched earth, plague epidemics, devastated towns, and crushing military taxes (porció and forspont) imposed by imperial troops quartered across Hungarian villages.

stories.title: Csalódás és elégedetlenség a felszabadulás után
stories.summary: Vienna treated Hungary as a conquered province rather than a liberated partner. The Neoacquistica Commission demanded exorbitant redemption fees from Hungarian nobles, while the Diet of 1687 revoked the hereditary right to elect kings and the right of armed resistance.

stories.title: A kuruc mozgalom és a Rákóczi-szabadságharc hajnala
stories.summary: The smoldering resentment gave birth to the Kuruc insurgent movement. When young Prince Ferenc Rákóczi II answered the call of the peasants in 1703, Hungary launched its greatest struggle for independence under the banner 'Cum Deo pro Patria et Libertate'.

stories.title: A török kiűzése és Magyarország új korszaka (1686–1699)
stories.summary: The dramatic liberation of Hungary from Ottoman rule (1686–1699): the heroic storming of Buda Castle on September 2, 1686 by the Holy League, crushing victories at Nagyharsány and Zenta, the milestone 1699 Peace of Karlowitz, the devastating economic toll of war on common folk, imperial absolutism and noble grievances, and the rise of the Kuruc rebellion under Prince Ferenc Rákóczi II.

stories.title: A Liget Budapest: új múzeumok a városligetben
stories.summary: Adapted and simplified from Wikipedia articles on the Városliget park and the Liget Budapest museum project, for A2 learners.
